summary:
DATUM-4 is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to help future astronauts navigate the Martian surface safely and efficiently.

Exploring Mars presents unique challenges: dangerous terrain, limited oxygen, communication delays, and rapidly changing environmental conditions. Existing planetary maps provide valuable scientific data, but translating that information into practical decisions during a Marswalk remains difficult.

DATUM-4 addresses this problem by bringing terrain analysis, scientific information, route planning, and mission safety indicators into one interactive interface. Users can explore the Martian surface, identify scientifically valuable destinations, assess potential hazards, and evaluate routes based on environmental conditions and mission constraints.

Our solution focuses on transforming complex planetary data into clear, actionable information that supports faster and more informed decisions.

DATUM-4 is more than a map of Mars. It is a step toward safer, smarter, and more independent human exploration of another planet.
details:
DATUM-4 is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning platform designed to support safer and more efficient human exploration of the Martian surface. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, our project transforms complex planetary data into practical tools that help astronauts navigate, assess risks, and make informed decisions.

How It Works

DATUM-4 integrates interactive 2D and 3D maps with scientific datasets, terrain analysis, and intelligent route-planning algorithms.

Our prototype focuses on Gale Crater, near Mount Sharp, using planetary elevation models, orbital imagery, and data from NASA's Curiosity mission.

Users can explore locations, select scientific destinations, and calculate routes using four optimization modes: FASTEST, SAFEST, BALANCED, and SCIENCE.

The route-planning system evaluates terrain elevation, slope, surface roughness, estimated travel time, environmental hazards, and mission constraints. It also estimates return-to-base safety margins and classifies route feasibility using three indicators: READY, CAUTION, and NO_GO.

Additional capabilities include Martian time calculations, solar positioning, Earth-Mars communication delay estimates, orbital communication analysis, and navigation methods that do not depend on GPS.

Technology and Development

Our technical architecture combines:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, OpenLayers, Three.js.
  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Numba.
  • Geospatial processing: Rasterio, PyProj, digital elevation models.
  • Navigation: A* pathfinding, terrain-based risk assessment, route optimization.
  • Scientific data: NASA MOLA, Curiosity mission datasets, USGS planetary maps, and Mars24 calculations.

The project uses mathematical models, automated testing, and documented scientific data sources to support reproducibility and transparency.

Innovation and Impact

Unlike conventional planetary visualization tools, DATUM-4 focuses on translating scientific information into operational decisions.

Our innovation lies in combining terrain navigation, environmental risk assessment, mission-resource constraints, and return-to-base planning within one interactive system.

During development, our team prioritized astronaut safety, scientific accuracy, clear visualization, transparent assumptions, and usability under stressful conditions.

DATUM-4 is a research prototype rather than a certified mission-navigation system. Its long-term goal is to demonstrate how integrated planetary data and computational tools could support future astronauts, mission planners, and researchers.

We believe the future of space exploration requires more than accurate maps. It requires systems that help humans understand risks, evaluate alternatives, and make safer decisions far from Earth.
